title: What If High Schools Started an Hour Later? Seattle Tried It

scenes.text: What if high schools started an hour later? Seattle tried it, and scientists measured the sleep.
In 2016, Seattle moved its high school start times from 7:50 to 8:45 in the morning.
Students gained a median of 34 extra minutes of sleep every school night, tracked with wrist monitors.
Their median sleep rose from about 6 hours 50 minutes to 7 hours 24 minutes.
Biology grades rose 4.5 percent, and tardies and first-period absences fell at the school that had struggled with them.
The study cannot prove sleep caused the grades. But the extra half hour of sleep was real, and it was measured.
